chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUqbah, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said:
I saw Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام enter the grave, and he did not undo his buttons.
So the proper understanding of this report is the lifting of prohibition from one who does not undo his buttons, because doing that is among the recommended acts, not the obligatory ones.

key_terms.أَزْرَارَهُ: his buttons or fastenings on his garment
key_terms.الْقَبْرَ: the grave, in the context of burial rites
key_terms.الْمَسْنُونَاتِ: recommended acts established in the sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.الْوَاجِبَاتِ: obligatory acts that are legally required

ai.seo_question: Is undoing one’s buttons when entering the grave obligatory or only recommended in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report concerns the etiquettes related to entering the grave during burial. It indicates that undoing one’s buttons is recommended rather than obligatory, and that leaving them fastened does not entail prohibition.
